The ported cases run in 2 Boost.Test suites, cases and actors_cases, declared with webcpp.boost-test, which read the fixture files and register one test case for each case, so that a failure names its case. A wasm program cannot read them without a directory its runtime opens for it, so these suites run natively only:

Suite What it checks

cases

Every machine case, one test case each, against XState’s record.

actors_cases

Every actor case, one test case each, against XState’s record, actor by actor.

cases runs a case as a caller that pays fuel runs a machine: each macrostep through the cursor, one microstep a call, at most 10,000 of them, exactly one of which must say it settled. It writes each microstep as the oracle writes it, the event, the transitions, the actions and the snapshot (value, context, status, output, error, tags sorted, children, and the active nodes in order), and compares every step with XState’s. It also compares the machine’s definition, to_json, with XState’s machine.toJSON(), and where that definition holds the whole machine, it loads the machine back from it and runs the case again. actors_cases runs each actor case on an actor_system and compares, after every step, what each actor did with what XState’s did, under the keys the oracle writes. In both, a case file without XState’s output, or an output file that is not one, fails its cases rather than vanishing.

Beside them, test/Jamfile compiles each of the 24 public headers alone, as the only include of its translation unit, so that a header that leans on an include it does not make fails, naming it. core_alone checks that the machine core includes nothing of xactor or of the actor layer, every include guard of theirs still undefined after <webcpp/xstate.hpp>; and user_aggregates compiles a user’s designated initializers that leave members out, as the user’s own code, with -Wextra and warnings as errors.

While working on one test, build and run it alone; before saying a change is done, run every test from scratch, and then the oracle:

b2 libs/xstate/test//cases
b2 -a libs/xstate/test libs/xstate/example
b2 -a libs/xstate/test/oracle//oracle

The examples

Every program this page shows is a test. b2 libs/xstate/example builds each program of example/xstate/ and example/actors/, declared in example/Jamfile with webcpp.example, runs it, and compares what it printed on the standard output, every carriage return removed, with the <name>.expected committed beside it, through webcpp’s tools/example/run_example.py. A difference fails the build with a diff. So does a program that returns anything but 0, even when it printed the expected lines, since each program returns 1 when a check of its own fails. Every run compares again, whatever b2 holds up to date, so a run never passes on the result of an earlier one.

The same programs build for wasm32-wasip2 and wasm32-wasip3, and run under wasmtime, through which run_example.py runs each (Targets). A program’s output is compared with the same <name>.expected on every target, so it prints the same on every target, each of which builds it with exceptions.

b2 libs/xstate/doc builds this page from the same files, each program’s source included by tag and its output whole, so neither can drift from the library. Any message of Asciidoctor’s fails it, a reference to no section among them, and so does an output whose program is gone, a program the page does not show, or the output of a twin that diverges that the page does not show.

Regenerating XState’s output

XState’s output is committed: the oracle’s under test/fixtures/expected/ and test/fixtures/actors/expected/, and that of each twin that diverges beside the twin (The XState twins). After a case is added or changed, or a twin that diverges, update-expected runs the scripts on every case and replaces the committed output with what they write, then rewrites the output of every twin that diverges with what XState prints. Its diff is what XState does, and so what the suites and this page will hold xstate to; read it, then run the suites. It needs Node.

b2 libs/xstate/test/oracle//update-expected

The oracle lane runs the same scripts into its build directory, compares what they wrote with the committed output, file by file and byte by byte, through webcpp’s tools/oracle/compare.py, and fails when the two differ; it also runs the twins against the outputs committed beside them. A case changed without its output, or an output edited by hand, fails the lane, so the committed expectations are always what XState 5.33.2 produces for the committed cases. The oracle lane is the one place xstate’s tests need Node; b2 libs/xstate/test does not, and never runs npm.

Guarantees

What xstate promises whatever its caller does: the rules its results keep, which the sections above teach and the tests check. A guarantee keeps its number, and the anchor named after it, so a comment of the code or of a test cites it by that anchor: (doc: #xstate-invariant-13) sends its reader to the thirteenth guarantee, and (doc: #xstate-invariant-a3) to the third of the actor layer. b2 libs/xstate/doc, which builds this page, fails on a citation that names no anchor of it (How xstate is tested). What xactor promises, which the actor layer builds on, is on xactor’s page.

The machine core

  1. A machine is created once from its config and never changes. A config’s states, on and after are read in the order JavaScript enumerates an object’s keys, as XState reads them: a key that is an array index, such as "0" or "500", first, by number, then the rest as written. That order is the document order of the states, the order of a state’s transitions and the order of the raises its after schedules. Creating a machine refuses each of these, with an error and no machine; create_machine gives the code of each, and What creation refuses shows them:

    • a config that is not an object, or a member of the wrong type, such as an invoke’s id or systemId that is not a string;

    • a compound state without initial;

    • an initial or a target that names no state, but for a history at the root, which XState accepts and so does xstate (guarantee 23);

    • an on key of "";

    • a transition that declares a truthy cond, renamed guard in XState v5, whose development build refuses it;

    • a guard, or a named delay of an after key, that the implementations do not hold, where a raise’s or a send’s named delay that they do not hold is no delay, as in XState;

    • an after key that starts with a digit, ., - or + and is not a whole number of milliseconds, such as "1.5" or "5abc" (Time in whole milliseconds);

    • a node whose default entry leads back to it, such as a history whose default target is an ancestor whose initial chain reaches the history again;

    • an invoke whose src is not a string (An invoke’s src), and an actor the implementations do not hold (guarantee 22);

    • an entry, exit or actions that is null, which XState’s toArray reads as a list that holds null and throws on when it runs it;

    • a history’s target that is neither a string nor a list of strings, the root’s included: XState reads a null one the same way and throws on it where it needs the default, and takes any other as it is (A config is refused when it is created);

    • a tags that holds anything but strings, null included;

    • implementations of which one holds an empty function (an assigner, an event, a value or an id maker, a guard, a delay or the context), which calling would abort without exceptions, where an optional one left out holds none; and an entry of implementations::inputs or implementations::outputs that names what it may not (guarantee 24).

  2. An action the implementations do not hold is a custom action. It is returned to the caller as {type, params}, in the order XState returns it, and the core does nothing else with it.

  3. assign changes the context, merging the partial update its implementation returns as Object.assign does, and is never returned as an action. raise, log, cancel, sendParent and the actions of guarantee 21 are returned with their resolved params, sendParent as XState’s xstate.sendTo to #_parent.

  4. A raise without a numeric delay goes to the macrostep’s internal queue; one with a delay is only returned, for the caller’s clock.

  5. A state with after raises xstate.after.<delay>.<id>, with that id and delay, on entry, and cancels it on exit, as XState does.

  6. One call of next() runs exactly one microstep. The first runs the external event’s microstep, or, for the initial macrostep, the initial one; each later call runs one iteration of XState’s macrostep loop.

  7. progress::settled is true on the microstep after which XState’s macrostep loop would stop, and on no other: when no eventless transition is enabled and no raised event is queued, or the status is not active. An external event that selects no transition settles on the first next(), with the snapshot unchanged, unless an eventless transition is enabled after it, as a guard that reads the event can make it, or the event is an actor’s error event, which guarantee 20 settles in error. An external event of the type * is refused: the first next() fails the macrostep with invalid_event, as XState’s development build refuses it, while an event of that type the machine raises takes the wildcard transitions.

  8. The core never stops a macrostep: an always cycle never settles, and the caller’s fuel is the only bound. A cursor is a value, and a copy resumes exactly where the original stopped.

  9. Eventless transitions are selected after the first microstep of a macrostep, the initial one or the external event’s, and after every microstep of a raised event, whatever it changed. After a microstep of eventless transitions they are selected again only when it changed the snapshot: the active nodes, the history, the context (an assign ran), the children (a spawn or a stop resolved, guarantee 18) or the status. This is XState’s comparison of snapshots by identity, stated as a rule: its loop selects them again when the microstep returned another snapshot than the one it began from.

  10. The active nodes are an insertion-ordered set: kept nodes keep their place, exited nodes leave it, and entered nodes are appended in document order. A microstep that ends with the same active nodes and history keeps the order it had, as XState returns its snapshot unchanged; any other microstep that leaves the machine done lists them by descending order instead, each after its descendants, as XState sorts its array of active nodes in place when the machine is done. That order decides which eventless transition a parallel region takes first. A state value’s keys are in the order JavaScript enumerates them, as XState’s value is an object: array indices first, by number, then the rest in the order of the nodes.

  11. An implementation’s failure sets the snapshot’s status to error, with its error code, and settles the macrostep. The failing microstep reports no actions, as XState’s pure functions throw, and neither does the macrostep’s result for it; its progress::resolved_before_failure holds the actions it resolved before the failure, which a running actor of XState has run in part (guarantee A9).

  12. Every result equals XState’s for the same machine and events: each microstep’s event, transitions, actions and snapshot (value, context, status, output, tags, active nodes in order), as the oracle records them in test/fixtures/expected/ (XState as the oracle).

  13. simulated_clock releases due events by (deadline, scheduling order), one at a time, and cannot be set back in time.

  14. to_json (The definition) writes XState’s definition of the machine, key for key, plus the higher-order guards XState cannot write. XState’s definition leaves out the context, the eventless transitions and a history state’s default target, and two states may share an id when a key holds a dot. A machine created from a definition, given its context, takes the original’s steps and writes the same definition, its version included, whenever none of those is in the original and no entry or exit names a custom action xstate.raise or xstate.cancel, which a definition cannot tell from the raise and the cancel an after adds. A definition XState would not write, one with a member of another type than XState writes, such as an entry or an exit that is not a list, is invalid_config.

  15. xstate throws no exception of its own: every operation that can fail returns a result, and the library compiles without exceptions, which the lint checks for every public header and for every test and example, which instantiate its templates. It holds no global or static mutable state, and it never reads a clock, a file or a network.

  16. A machine starts with an input, null when none. The event xstate.init carries a non-null input as its member input. When implementations::context is set, the initial context is what it returns for the input, in place of the config’s context; a failure, or a value that is not an object, fails the initial macrostep on its first next(), with the snapshot before it (XState’s _getPreInitialState).

  17. A state’s invoke, one object or a list, names a child actor by its string src, with an optional id, by default <index>.<state id> (XState’s createInvokeId), input and systemId. Its onDone, onError and onSnapshot are transitions on xstate.done.actor.<id>, xstate.error.actor.<id> and xstate.snapshot.<id>. A node’s transitions are kept in XState’s Map order: on, onDone, each invoke’s three, after; a descriptor given twice keeps its first place and its last transitions, except under after, whose transitions append.

  18. Entering a state returns, after its entry actions and before its initial actions, one xstate.spawnChild per invoke, its params {id, src, input?, systemId?}, and adds the child to the snapshot’s children; exiting it returns, after its exit actions, one xstate.stopChild per invoke, its params {id}, and removes the child, with no params when the child is no longer there. Both change the snapshot, as guarantee 9 counts change. The core runs no child: its caller does. children lists (id, src) in the order JavaScript enumerates XState’s children object: ids that are array indices first, by number, then the others in spawning order.

  19. A macrostep whose snapshot is not active when it settles, done or still in the error it began from, returns, after every microstep’s actions, one xstate.stopChild per child left, in macrostep_result::actions and in no microstep; the snapshot keeps its children (XState’s stopChildren, whose snapshot XState drops). A macrostep that guarantee 20 settles, or one that fails, returns none.

  20. An external event whose type starts with xstate.error.actor and that selects no transition settles in one microstep, with an empty list of transitions and no action: the snapshot the macrostep began from, its status error, its error actor_failed and its error_value the event’s member error, when it has one. Its children stay, and no xstate.stopChild is returned (XState’s macrostep).

  21. The actions that name other actors are registered by name and returned with XState’s params: spawn_child_action as xstate.spawnChild {id, src, input?, systemId?}, adding the child; stop_child_action as xstate.stopChild, as in guarantee 18; send_to_action and forward_to_action, which sends the microstep’s event, as xstate.sendTo {targetId, event, id?, delay?}; emit_action as xstate.emit {event}. A sendTo’s target is #_parent, #_internal, #system:<systemId>, #_<id> or <id>; a child it names must be in the snapshot’s children when the action resolves, or, named <id> by an entry or initial action, be an invoke of the state being entered (XState’s deferredActorIds); otherwise the microstep fails with unknown_target. A sendTo naming an invoke of the state being entered by its bare id carries action::bound_at: how many of its microstep’s actions come before the point where XState binds it to the child that id names, the end of that state’s entry actions, spawns and initial actions (XState’s retryResolveSendTo); any other action has none.

  22. Every actor a machine names, an invoke’s src or the src of a spawn_child_action the config names as an action, is an entry of implementations::actors; creating the machine refuses any other with unknown_actor. A registered spawn_child_action the config never names is not checked, as XState’s setup accepts it.

  23. A history at the root has no parent to resolve its default against. When its target is absent, a string or a list of strings, the machine is created, as XState creates it, and a microstep that needs the default, the initial one or one that enters the root or reaches it through another history’s default, fails with unknown_target, where XState’s resolveHistoryDefaultTransition throws. A target that is an empty list names nothing, and the root enters nothing below it, as in XState. Creating the machine refuses a target of any other type (guarantee 1).

  24. A value an implementation computes, the value a log logs, an invoke’s input (implementations::inputs, by the invoke’s id), a spawn’s input or a final state’s output (implementations::outputs, by the state’s id, the root’s id for the machine’s), may be none, JavaScript’s undefined: the member is left out, as XState leaves it out, so the log has no value, the child no input and the snapshot no output. An input is computed when its state is entered, after the state’s entry actions; a final state’s output from the context and the event that entered it, and the machine’s from the done event of the final state that completed it, as XState’s getMachineOutput computes it. Creating the machine refuses, with invalid_config, an input that names no invoke or an output that names neither a final state nor the root, and one of either that the config also fixes.

The actor layer

The actor layer’s guarantees are numbered from A1, so that a citation tells them from the machine core’s.

A1

Every host call that delivers (start, send, clock_tick, resolve, reject, resume) opens executions of its own, each with the budget’s fuel, and runs the system until no message is left; it returns out_of_fuel when an actor is left parked, settled otherwise. While an actor is parked, start, send, clock_tick, resolve and reject are checked and then held, in the order made, and return out_of_fuel; resume(), once the parked actors have settled, applies them in that order, each run to its end before the next, as XState runs each of its host’s calls to its end. An answer whose request is no longer pending when it is applied is dropped, as XState ignores a promise that settles after its actor stopped. stop is never held: it is how the host ends an actor that would never settle.

A2

An actor runs one macrostep at a time. An event that arrives while a macrostep has not settled, or before the actor has started, waits; the waiting events run afterwards in the order they arrived, each its own macrostep (XState’s run to completion).

A3

Fuel: every microstep costs one unit of the execution’s fuel, paid before it runs, and so does every message an actor sends (an event, a child’s construction and its reply, a child’s start, a stop) and every timer it arms. When the execution cannot pay, the actor parks with what it has not done; resume() gives each parked actor a new execution and continues it there. A parked actor never runs a microstep or an effect it has not paid for, nor one twice, and does nothing until its resume, so it stays parked only while something is left to do.

A4

Construction and start, after XState’s createActor and start(): an actor’s construction runs its initial macrostep, resolving its actions (A5); its start then hands over the custom actions and logs that macrostep returned and runs what it deferred (A6), the starts of its active children first, as XState’s start() starts the snapshot’s active children and then runs the actor’s initial actions. A child born done or failed starts where its spawn put it. A child is constructed when its parent resolves its spawnChild, and started when the parent’s macrostep has settled; the root is constructed and started by the host’s start. A construction that fails drops what it would have handed over and deferred; the start then fails the actor (A9).

A5

Resolution: as each microstep is computed, the actor resolves its actions in order, as XState’s resolveActionsAndContext does, then the stopChild actions the macrostep returns after its microsteps (guarantee 19):

  • a custom action reaches on_action, and xstate.log on_log;

  • xstate.spawnChild claims its systemId, if any, and creates the child implementations::actors names for its src, a machine actor or a host actor, with its input. A machine child is constructed at once (A4), and the actor waits until it is, so the children of its initial macrostep exist and their systemIds are registered when the next action resolves, as XState’s createActor constructs a child inside resolveSpawn. Its start is deferred;

  • xstate.stopChild releases the systemIds the child and its descendants hold, and the actor forgets the child. A child this macrostep created, which has not started, is stopped at once and never starts; the stop of a started child is deferred. In the initial macrostep all of it is deferred, as XState runs every initial action on start();

  • xstate.sendTo resolves its target now: a child by id or #_<id>, the parent (#_parent), the actor itself (#_internal), or the actor registered under a systemId (#system:<id>, the actor itself when none is, but for a forwardTo, which fails the actor with unknown_target there, as XState’s development build throws). One that carries bound_at (guarantee 21) is bound to the child its id names once that many of the microstep’s actions are resolved, as XState’s retryResolveSendTo binds it, and fails the actor when it is delivered if no child had that id then. Its delivery, or its timer, is deferred;

  • a delayed raise, xstate.cancel and xstate.emit are deferred.

A6

Deferred effects: when its macrostep has settled and every action is resolved, the actor publishes its snapshot (snapshot_of) and runs what the resolution deferred, in order: deliveries and timers, cancels, emits, the stops of started children, the starts of created ones. A started child asked to stop receives the request behind everything already sent it, so it finishes the macrostep it runs and the events that arrived before, ignores what arrives after, asks each of its own children to stop the same way, and stops, running no exit action; a child that has already ended ignores it, and its children keep running, as in XState. The actor then notifies its subscribers when its snapshot is active or done (an empty listener is none, as an empty callback is), releases its systemId if it is done or failed, as XState’s _stopProcedure does even when the report waits for fuel, and reports to its parent: xstate.done.actor.<id> {output, actorId} when done, xstate.error.actor.<id> {error, actorId} when failed, the error being the actor’s error_value (a child’s error climbs unchanged) or the name of its error code.

A7

A delayed raise or sendTo arms a timer owned by its sender, under its id when it has one. A timer armed under an id is the one a cancel of that id finds until another is armed under it or any timer of that id fires; an earlier one under the same id still fires, as XState’s scheduler keeps its timeout and its timerMap names the latest. clock_tick(now) releases the timers due by now one at a time, in (deadline, arming) order, and runs after each, all in one execution, so a timer’s handling can cancel a later one of the same tick, or take its id over, as XState’s SimulatedClock fires them; one armed meanwhile and due by now is released in the same call. When an actor parks, the rest of the tick is held first in line (A1), so no timer fires for a parked actor. A delayed sendTo is forwarded by its sender when the timer fires, in the order the timers fire; a retired actor’s timers never fire.

A8

A systemId names one actor from its creation until the actor is done, failed or stopped, or until a stopChild releases it or one of its ancestors (A5): get finds it, and a claim of it fails the claiming actor (A9). A done or failed actor releases it at once, even while its report waits for fuel (A6), and a child whose construction leaves it done or failed releases its own then, as XState’s constructor does. When its parent starts it, the start fails the parent with system_id_taken if a child the parent’s macrostep created, or one descended from it, holds the name then, as XState’s start() claims it again and throws; it is a deferred effect that fails (A9). XState runs each start and each send of the macrostep’s deferred effects nested, before the next, so a sibling that ends during its own start has released the name by then, and an actor a deferred send reached may have claimed it; here those run later, in turns of their own, so the check sees the names as the macrostep’s own children hold them, and the outcome can differ (Interleaving across actors).

A9

What XState throws for while resolving, a claim of a systemId that is held and a sendTo to the parent of a root, fails the actor there: no later action of the macrostep is handed over or resolved, nothing it deferred runs, the children it created are stopped, and the snapshot is the one the macrostep began from, its status error and its error system_id_taken or unknown_target. What was handed over before stays handed over; the started children it asked to stop are the actor’s again, as the snapshot it falls back to lists them. A microstep that fails, by an implementation or a history at the root, first has the actions it resolved before the failure resolved as any, as a running actor of XState has run them: custom actions and logs are handed over, and a spawn’s claim of a held systemId fails first; then the resolution ends the same way, with the snapshot of guarantee 11. An initial macrostep hands over none of them, as XState runs those on start(). A deferred effect that fails fails the actor with the snapshot its macrostep reached, which an inspector hears as XState’s update inspects it, and the children the macrostep created that have not started are stopped; a start’s active children have.

A10

A host actor is created when its spawnChild resolves and, once started, is a pending host_request; resolve and reject end it, done or failed, and its parent receives its done or error event. A request whose actor has ended is no longer pending, and resolve or reject of it is invalid_argument and changes nothing.

A11

A failed actor’s children keep running, as in XState; a done actor’s were stopped by the stopChild its last macrostep returned. stop stops a root actor and its family from the host, at once; for a child it is invalid_argument and changes nothing, as XState’s actor.stop() refuses a child.

A12

The host’s callbacks, a subscribe or on_emitted listener, the on_action and on_log callbacks and the inspector, run inside an actor’s turn. A call from one of them that changes the system is invalid_argument and changes nothing; the const ones, which read it, are free. subscribe and on_emitted add a listener of one actor, called in the order added, and refuse an address that names no actor with invalid_argument, as start and send do; on_action, on_log and inspect hold one callback for the whole system, which a later call replaces; an empty callback is none.

Reference

Every name xstate declares, in the namespace webcpp::xstate, from the Doc Comments of its headers: each class, function, type and enumerator with its declaration, what it does, what it asks of its caller and how it fails, and the part of XState 5.33.2 it ports. The other sections teach the library; this one is where a name is looked up. XState’s names, in From XState to C++, goes the other way, from XState’s names to xstate’s.

A clock the caller owns, which holds the delayed events of the machine core until the time it is set to reaches them.

webcpp::xstate::action

An action returned to the caller to execute.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actions.hpp>

struct action;

Description

It ports XState’s ExecutableActionObject. A custom action (builtin false) has the type the config named and the params it gave, null when it gave none. A built-in one was resolved by xstate, and params holds what it resolved: an event in XState’s flat form, a delay in milliseconds.

Each built-in type is returned for these actions, with these params:

  • xstate.raise, for a raise_action and on entering a state with after, its params event, id when it has one and delay when delayed;

  • xstate.cancel, for a cancel_action and on leaving a state with after, its params sendId;

  • xstate.log, for a log_action, its params value unless undefined and label when it has one;

  • xstate.sendTo, for a send_to_action, a send_parent_action and a forward_to_action, its params targetId, event, id when it has one and delay when delayed;

  • xstate.emit, for an emit_action, its params event;

  • xstate.spawnChild, for a spawn_child_action and on entering a state that invokes, its params id, src, and input and systemId when there are any;

  • xstate.stopChild, for a stop_child_action, on leaving a state that invokes, and for each child left when a macrostep settles not active, its params id, or null when the child was not there.

An assign is never returned.

Note

builtin tells the two kinds apart, not the type: a config may name an action xstate.sendTo and give it no implementation, and it is returned as a custom action all the same, which simulated_clock::apply ignores.

Whether the action is a forwardTo’s sendTo.

webcpp::xstate::actor_system

A system of actors on one xactor scheduler, run by its host.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

class actor_system;

Description

It ports XState’s createActor and its actor system in one. Its scheduler, a webcpp::xactor::scheduler, holds one first-in first-out mailbox per actor and one first-in first-out queue of the actors that have work, and each turn hands one message to its actor, so a message an actor sends is queued, never handled inside the sender’s turn. The host creates actors from machines, which runs nothing. Then it starts them, sends them events, brings the time and answers the host actors: each of these calls, and actor_system::resume, runs the system until no message is left, as XState’s send() processes at once, and returns a run_outcome. stop stops a family at once and returns it. The system is neither copied nor moved, since every actor holds a reference to its shared state, and one thread runs it.

Every refusal is webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument, of the category "webcpp.xactor", but one: create_actor refuses a systemId another actor holds with xstate’s own errc::system_id_taken, of the category "webcpp.xstate". xstate’s errc has no invalid_argument. The readers refuse nothing: snapshot_of, parent_of, id_of, get and child_of answer nullptr, none or an empty view for what they do not find.

While an actor is parked, start, send, clock_tick, resolve and reject are checked, then held in the order made, and return run_outcome::out_of_fuel; actor_system::resume applies them once the parked actors have settled, each run to its end before the next, as XState runs each of its host’s calls to its end. stop is never held.

The host’s callbacks, the listeners of subscribe and on_emitted, those of on_action and on_log, and the inspector, run inside an actor’s turn, while the system runs. A call from one of them to a member that changes the system, a registration included, returns webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument and changes nothing; the const members, which read the system, are free. XState accepts a send from a subscriber and handles it after the update in progress. An empty std::function is no callback.

webcpp::xstate::actor_system::clock_tick

Moves the system’s time to now, releasing the timers due by then.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

result<run_outcome>
clock_tick(uint64_t now);

Description

It releases them one at a time, in (deadline, arming) order, and runs the system after each, all in one execution, whose fuel bounds a chain of timers that keep arming. A timer armed meanwhile and due by now is released in the same call, where XState’s may not be. A delayed sendTo is forwarded by its sender when its timer fires. When an actor parks, the rest of the tick is held first in line, so no timer fires for a parked actor.

A time earlier than the last tick’s is not refused: the system’s time moves back to it, and a timer armed afterwards falls due that much earlier. simulated_clock::set refuses the same move, and XState’s SimulatedClock.set throws.

Note

One at a time, as XState’s SimulatedClock fires them, so a timer’s handling can cancel a later one of the same tick, or take its id over.

Return Value

The outcome of the run; webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument from a callback.

Parameters

Name Description

now

The time, in milliseconds.

See Also

"Delayed events and time", in the guide.

"A timer that falls due during clock_tick", in the guide.

"A tick earlier than the last", in the guide.

"Guarantees", in the guide: guarantee A7.

webcpp::xstate::actor_system::create_actor

Creates an actor that runs a machine, not yet started.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

result<xactor::actor_ref>
create_actor(
    machine const& logic,
    actor_options const& options = {});

Description

It ports XState’s createActor. Unlike XState’s, the actor’s construction, which runs its initial macrostep, happens on start, so until then snapshot_of returns nullptr and get finds none of its children’s systemIds. The actor holds its systemId from its creation, before it starts, until it is done, fails or is stopped. The roots of one system share their systemIds, where XState gives each root a system of its own.

Return Value

The actor’s address; errc::system_id_taken when an actor of the system holds options.system_id, which creates nothing; or webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument from a callback.

webcpp::xstate::actor_system::on_action

Hands every custom action of every actor to a listener, with the actor that returned it.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

result<void>
on_action(system_state::action_listener listener);

Description

An action is handed over as its microstep is resolved, and an actor’s initial ones when it starts. A macrostep that fails hands over those it resolved before the failure, as a running actor of XState has run them, and none after an action XState would throw for. An initial macrostep that fails hands over none, as XState’s start of an actor whose initial snapshot failed runs none of its initial actions. This is how a custom action runs, since a JSON config holds no function. It replaces the previous listener, and an empty one removes it.

Return Value

Success; webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument from a callback.

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

resolve(
    host_request const& request,

Description

The request’s host actor finishes done with output, and its parent receives xstate.done.actor.<id> with output and actorId. An answer held while an actor is parked is dropped if its request is no longer pending when it is applied, as XState ignores a promise that settles after its actor stopped; the call that held it has already returned run_outcome::out_of_fuel.

The outcome of the run; webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument, and nothing changes, when the request is no longer pending, its actor having been answered or stopped, or from a callback.

Stops a root actor and its whole family at once.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

stop(xactor::actor_ref actor);

Description

It ports XState’s actor.stop(). Each member is stopped after its descendants, the children of a failed member included, where XState’s leaves them running. No exit action runs, and a stopped actor’s timers never fire, where XState may still fire one.

Note

It is never held behind a parked actor, since stopping is how the host ends an actor that would never settle.

Return Value

The actors it stopped, each after its descendants; webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument, and nothing changes, for a child, which XState refuses to stop directly, for an address that names no actor, and from a callback.

webcpp::xstate::event

An event: its type, and the members that travel with it.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/event.hpp>

struct event;

Description

It ports XState’s EventObject. XState writes an event flat, {"type": "SUBMIT", "user": "ana"}; xstate keeps the type apart, and the rest is the payload, {"user": "ana"}, which every implementation reads as args.event.payload. A caller builds one as xstate::event{.type = "SUBMIT", .payload = {{"user", "ana"}}}.

xstate makes some events itself: xstate.init, which runs the initial macrostep; xstate.done.state.<id>, raised when the state <id> reaches a final state, with the final state’s output when it has one; xstate.after.<delay>.<id>, the delayed event of a state’s after; and, in the actor layer, xstate.done.actor.<id> and xstate.error.actor.<id>, which a child sends its parent when it ends.

Data Members

Name Description

payload

Every other member of the event, in the order it was written.

type

The type, which the transitions’ event descriptors match.

webcpp::xstate::guard_node

A guard as the config names it: a registered guard, by name, with its params, or one of XState’s higher-order guards.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/state_node.hpp>

struct guard_node;

Description

XState’s higher-order guards are functions, which xstate’s JSON writes as {"type": "xstate.not", "guards": [g]}, xstate.and and xstate.or over a list of guards, and {"type": "xstate.stateIn", "stateValue": v}. and stops at its first false operand and or at its first true one. stateIn holds when the snapshot matches its state_value, or, for a string #id, when the node with that id is active.

Note

A machine keeps its guards in one flat list (machine::guard), and a higher-order guard names its operands by their index there, so a guard nested as deep as its JSON is held and evaluated without recursion.

webcpp::xstate::host_logic

The logic of a host actor, in place of XState’s fromPromise.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/host_logic.hpp>

class host_logic final
    : public xactor::actor_logic<actor_message>

Description

Once started, it is a pending host_request with its input. The host’s answer ends it: done with the answer as its output, its parent receiving xstate.done.actor.<id> with output and actorId; or failed with the answer as its error, its parent receiving xstate.error.actor.<id> with error and actorId, and its turn returning errc::actor_failed, so its xactor status is error. Answered, it releases its systemId before it reports. It ignores every other event, as XState’s promise actor does. machine_logic creates one when an invoke or a spawnChild names a host_actor; a host does not construct it.

webcpp::xstate::implementations

The implementations a machine is created with, each registered by the name its config gives it.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/implementations.hpp>

struct implementations;

Description

It ports XState’s setup({ actions, actors, guards, delays }). A JSON config cannot hold a function, so it names each implementation, and an implementations maps the names to C++ functions; create_machine takes it with the config. An empty one, {}, makes every action of the config a custom action, and holds no guard, delay or actor.

create_machine refuses, with errc::invalid_config, implementations that hold an empty std::function, which a program without exceptions could not call; an entry of inputs that names no invoke, or one whose config has an input; and an entry of outputs that names neither a final state nor the root, or one whose config has an output.

webcpp::xstate::inspector

What an inspector hears, after XState’s inspect.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/system_state.hpp>

struct inspector;

Description

It hears each actor’s start, each macrostep a machine actor settles, with the event that began it, and each event an actor emits. actor_system::inspect takes it, and an empty member is none. A macrostep that settles with the error errc::actor_failed, which an unhandled xstate.error.actor.<id> event gives, is heard with that snapshot.

Note

A macrostep that fails where XState throws is not heard, as XState inspects no snapshot for an actor whose transition threw. That is every failure of its cursor but errc::actor_failed (macrostep::next lists them): an implementation’s own failure; errc::implementation_failed from a built-in assign on a context that is not an object, or from a context function whose value is not one; errc::unknown_state for a value or a stateIn id that names no state; errc::invalid_event for an event of the type *; and errc::unknown_target for a sendTo the core finds naming no actor, or for the default of a history state that is the machine’s root. Nor is one that fails while its actions resolve (a systemId taken, a target that names no actor). One a deferred effect fails, a send bound to a child that is gone, is heard with the snapshot it reached, as XState’s update inspects it.

Hears an actor’s start, with the actor’s address.

webcpp::xstate::machine

The immutable tree of state nodes create_machine builds from a config, with the implementations it was given.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/machine.hpp>

class machine;

Description

It ports XState’s StateMachine. Only create_machine makes one, so machine has no default constructor. It is a handle to data nothing changes once created: a copy is cheap and shares that data, and a cursor, an actor and a machine_actor each keep one.

Nodes are numbered in document order: the root 0, a parent before its children, and siblings in the order JavaScript enumerates the keys of states. The number is XState’s order unless two nodes share an id (state_node::order). Everything names a node by that index (snapshot::nodes, transition_definition::target), so the tree holds no pointer and copies as a value.

webcpp::xstate::machine_logic

The logic of a machine actor, XState’s createActor for a machine.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/machine_logic.hpp>

class machine_logic final
    : public xactor::actor_logic<actor_message>

Description

Each message is one turn. The actor keeps its snapshot and runs one macrostep at a time with the macrostep cursor, paying one unit of fuel a microstep. It resolves each microstep’s actions as the microstep is computed, and runs what they deferred (deliveries and timers, cancels, emits, the stops and starts of children) once the macrostep has settled. When its execution cannot pay, it parks with what it has not done, and only a resume continues it, so no event starts before the macrostep in progress has settled and no work runs unpaid or twice.

It ends done when its machine is done, after its parent has received its done event, and fails when a macrostep, or an effect it deferred, fails, after its parent has received its error event. That event, xstate.error.actor.<id>, carries as error the actor’s error_value, unchanged, when an unhandled error event failed it (errc::actor_failed), and no error when that event carried none. Otherwise it carries the name of the actor’s error code, its message(), such as "implementation_failed". Its turn then returns the failure, and its xactor status is error. actor_system::create_actor creates one, and so does a machine actor for each invoke or spawnChild that names a machine_actor; a host does not construct it.

webcpp::xstate::macrostep

The cursor of one macrostep, which runs one microstep a call.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/macrostep.hpp>

class macrostep;

Description

It ports XState’s macrostep loop, one iteration a call. XState runs a macrostep to its end; the cursor lets its caller decide how much work an event may cost, one unit of fuel a call, and stop and resume where it likes. begin_initial and begin make one; it has no public constructor. A cursor is a value: it holds a copy of its machine, a handle, and of its snapshots and queue, so a copy resumes exactly where the original stopped, apart from it. xstate never stops a macrostep on its own: an always cycle never settles, and the caller’s fuel is the only bound.

webcpp::xstate::macrostep::next

Runs exactly one microstep.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/macrostep.hpp>

progress
next();

Description

It runs the initial microstep, the external event’s, or one iteration of XState’s loop, an enabled eventless transition first and a raised event otherwise. Once the macrostep has settled it runs nothing, and returns a settled progress with the current snapshot, no list of transitions and no actions.

It returns no error: a failure settles the macrostep with the snapshot it began from, its status status::error and the failure as its error. The failure is an implementation’s, with its own code, or one of these:

  • errc::unknown_target when a sendTo names no actor, or a microstep needs the default of a history state that is the machine’s root;

  • errc::implementation_failed when an assign runs on a context that is not an object, for example the context of a config whose context is 5;

  • errc::invalid_event when the external event’s type is *; - errc::unknown_state when the snapshot’s value names no state of the machine, or a stateIn guard’s #id names none;

  • the context function’s error, or errc::implementation_failed when its value is not an object, on the first call of an initial macrostep.

When the failure comes from a guard of an eventless transition, which the cursor evaluates after a microstep to know whether it settled, the call reports the microstep it ran, with its transitions and actions, and the failed snapshot. An external event whose type starts with xstate.error.actor and that no transition takes is no failure: it settles in one microstep with an empty list of transitions, the snapshot it began from, its status status::error, its error errc::actor_failed and its error_value the event’s member error.

Note

XState’s actor, too, keeps the snapshot from before a macrostep that threw.

Return Value

What the call did.

See Also

"When an implementation fails", in the guide.

webcpp::xstate::macrostep_result

A settled macrostep: its stable snapshot, every action its microsteps returned, and how many microsteps ran.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/macrostep.hpp>

struct macrostep_result;

Description

When the macrostep fails, snapshot is the snapshot it began from, with the status status::error. actions still holds the actions of the microsteps that completed before the failure, including the microstep after which an eventless guard failed, and microsteps counts them. Of those actions, a running actor of XState has executed the custom actions and logs, which it runs as each microstep is resolved, and none of the built-in ones (a sendTo, an emit, a spawnChild, the stopChild of a started child, a delayed raise, a cancel), whose effects it defers until the macrostep has settled and drops when it throws. XState’s actor executes none of an initial macrostep that fails, since it runs an actor’s initial actions when the actor starts, and the start of an actor whose initial snapshot failed runs none. The actor layer does the same, and a caller that stands for XState’s actor executes the same ones.

webcpp::xstate::send_to_action

A send of an event to another actor, named by a target string.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/implementations.hpp>

struct send_to_action;

Description

It ports XState’s sendTo(target, event, { id, delay }). The target is a string as XState reads one: a child’s id, or #_ followed by it; #_parent, the parent; #_internal, the actor itself; or #system: followed by a systemId, the actor registered under it. It is returned as xstate.sendTo, its params holding targetId, event, flat, and id and delay as a raise’s. The machine core delivers nothing: its caller does, or the actor layer.

The microstep fails with errc::unknown_target when the target names a child the snapshot does not hold, unless an entry or initial action names, by its bare id, an invoke of the state being entered: that sendTo carries action::bound_at. #_parent, #_internal and #system: targets are always accepted here; the actor layer resolves them.

Note

XState sends to a systemId through a function of the system, ({ system }) => system.get(id), which JSON cannot hold.

Data Members

Name Description

delay

The delay, none for a send at once.

event

Computes the event to send.

id

The id a cancel names a delayed send by.

target

The actor to send to, as the target string names it.

webcpp::xstate::simulated_clock

A clock the caller owns, which holds the delayed events of the machine core until the time it is set to reaches them.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/clock.hpp>

class simulated_clock;

Description

It ports XState’s SimulatedClock with its scheduler. The machine core never reads a clock: a delayed event comes back as an action, and a clock holds it until the time the caller sets reaches it. Time is in whole milliseconds, where XState’s takes fractions, and starts at 0. The actor layer keeps its timers in xactor instead.

Member Functions

Name Description

Applies to the clock a built-in action a step returned.

Forgets the event scheduled under an id, if the id still names one.

Moves the time forward.

The time.

Takes the earliest event whose time has come out of the clock.

Holds an event until a delay from now.

Sets the time, which never goes back.

See Also

"Delayed events and the simulated clock", in the guide.

"In the machine core", in the guide.

webcpp::xstate::simulated_clock::apply

Applies to the clock a built-in action a step returned.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/clock.hpp>

void
apply(action const& returned);

Description

A built-in xstate.raise with a delay is scheduled, under its id when it has one, and a built-in xstate.cancel cancels its sendId. A delayed built-in xstate.sendTo with an id, a sendParent’s included, is not the machine’s to receive, but holds its id until it comes due, as XState’s scheduler keys every delayed event by its id. A raise without a delay, which its macrostep already ran, and every other action are ignored.

Note

A custom action is ignored whatever its type, a config being free to name one xstate.raise: XState’s scheduler, too, holds only what its built-in actions schedule.

Parameters

Name Description

returned

An action a step returned.

webcpp::xstate::simulated_clock::pop_due

Takes the earliest event whose time has come out of the clock.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/clock.hpp>

std::optional<event>
pop_due();

Description

The earliest is by deadline, then by the order the events were scheduled in, a rule where XState leaves equal deadlines to its sort. The id it was scheduled under then cancels nothing, as XState’s firing timeout deletes its entry of timerMap. The caller delivers each due event as a macrostep of its own and applies what that returns before the next call, so an event it schedules or cancels is ordered as XState orders it.

Return Value

The event; none when no event is due.

See Also

"Equal deadlines", in the guide.

The active nodes, by index, in XState’s order.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/snapshot.hpp>

Description

A node kept active keeps its place, an exited one leaves, and entered ones are appended in document order. The order decides which eventless transition a parallel region takes first, and the order of the keys of the state value that are not array indices. A microstep that leaves the machine done lists the nodes by descending order, each after its descendants, because XState sorts its array of active nodes in place when the machine is done. resolve_state sorts nothing, done or not, as XState’s resolveState does not.

webcpp::xstate::spawn_child_action

A spawn of a child actor that lives until it is stopped or the machine is done.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/implementations.hpp>

struct spawn_child_action;

Description

It ports XState’s spawnChild(src, { id, systemId, input }). Resolving it adds the child, (id, src), to the snapshot’s children, a child already there under that id taking the new src, and returns xstate.spawnChild, its params holding id, src, and input and systemId when there are any. The machine core runs no child: its caller does, or the actor layer. create_machine refuses, with errc::unknown_actor, a spawnChild the config names whose src is not an actor of the implementations.

Note

XState keys a child spawned without an id "undefined", and a stopChild then leaves it there; an id left out here is "", and the child is keyed under it.

The actor hands over what its initial macrostep returned and runs what it deferred, the starts of its active children first: XState’s actor.start(). actor_system::start sends it to a root, and a parent to each child it created once its macrostep has settled.

See Also

"Guarantees", in the guide: guarantee A4.

webcpp::xstate::stop_actor

Asks an actor to stop with its family, once it has handled what its parent sent it before.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/message.hpp>

struct stop_actor;

Description

It is XState’s deferred stopChild, which runs after the sends of the same macrostep. The actor finishes the macrostep it runs and the events that arrived before, ignores what arrives after, asks each of its own children to stop the same way, and stops, running no exit action. A child that has already ended ignores it.

See Also

"Stopping a child", in the guide.

"Guarantees", in the guide: guarantee A6.

A stop of a child actor.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/implementations.hpp>

Description

It ports XState’s stopChild(id). It removes the child id from the snapshot’s children and is returned as xstate.stopChild, its params holding id, or null when the snapshot held no such child. The actor layer stops the child with its family; a stop runs no exit action.

webcpp::xstate::system_state

What an actor system knows beside xactor’s statuses, shared by every actor of the system.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/system_state.hpp>

class system_state;

Description

It holds each actor’s record, the registry of systemIds, the host’s pending requests, the parked actors and the host’s callbacks. An actor_system owns one, and its actors reach it through the reference their logic was built with. A host does not call it: its listener types name the callbacks actor_system takes, and its members serve machine_logic and host_logic.

Note

An actor reaches it only during its own turn, so the system’s single thread is the only one that ever touches it.

Type Aliases

Name Description

action_listener

The listener of every custom action, with the actor that returned it, which actor_system::on_action sets.

event_listener

A listener of an actor’s emitted events, which actor_system::on_emitted adds.

log_listener

The listener of every log, with the actor that returned it, which actor_system::on_log sets.

snapshot_listener

A listener of an actor’s snapshots, which actor_system::subscribe adds.

Member Functions

Name Description

act

Hands a custom action to the host’s action listener.

add

Records an actor, the host’s or a spawned one, and its systemId.

Records a child spawned by parent; a child already there under the same id is replaced in the parent’s children, as XState’s snapshot replaces it, and keeps running.

answered

Removes the pending request of a host actor the host has answered.

Adds a host actor’s pending request.

on_log

Sets the listener of every log, replacing the previous one.

parked

The parked actors.

Keeps the snapshot a machine actor settled in, which actor_system::snapshot_of returns.

webcpp::xstate::errc

The errors xstate reports, as boost::system::error_code values of the category error_category.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/errors.hpp>

enum class errc : int;

Description

The values start at 1, so an error_code of value 0, which a snapshot that has not failed holds, is no error. An errc converts to an error_code and compares with one: created.error() == xstate::errc::unknown_target.

There is no invalid_argument: the code with which the actor layer refuses a call, an address that names no actor, a stop of a child, a request no longer pending or a call made from a callback, is xactor’s webcpp::xactor::errc::invalid_argument, of the category "webcpp.xactor".

Members

Name Description

invalid_config

A config is not a machine, or an implementation or a clock was misused.

unknown_target

A target names no state, or a send names no actor.

It ports XState’s getInitialSnapshot and _getPreInitialState, one microstep a call: the initial microstep, which enters the initial states, then XState’s loop for the event xstate.init, which carries input as its member input when it is not null. webcpp::xstate::create_machine

Builds a machine from the JSON of XState’s createMachine config, with the implementations its names stand for.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/machine.hpp>

result<machine>
create_machine(
    boost::json::value const& config,
    implementations registry);

Description

It ports XState’s setup({ ... }).createMachine(config). A config is refused here, at once, with an error and no machine, including what XState refuses only later, when it first evaluates a guard, enters a state or runs a list of actions. Two things are checked only when they are used, as in XState: the #id of an xstate.stateIn guard, which fails the macrostep or can with errc::unknown_state, and the default of a history state that is the machine’s root, which has no parent to resolve it against and fails the microstep that needs it with errc::unknown_target. A machine whose root is a history state is accepted, as XState accepts it. A history state below the root, a child of the root included, resolves its default against its parent.

A config’s states, on and after are read in the order JavaScript enumerates an object’s keys, as XState reads them: a key that is an array index, such as "0" or "500", first, by number, then the rest as written. That order is the document order of the states, and so the order in which a parallel state’s regions are entered; the order of a state’s transitions; and the order of the raises its after returns on entry, so an after that writes "1000" before "500" returns the raise of 500 first.

It fails with one of these errors:

  • errc::invalid_config when the config is not an object or a member has the wrong type; an entry or an exit, or the actions of a transition or of an object initial, is null, which XState’s toArray reads as a list that holds null and fails on when it runs it; a tags, or a history state’s target, is neither a string nor a list of strings, null included, the target of a history at the root too; a compound state has no initial; an on key is ""; a transition declares a truthy cond, renamed guard in XState v5; an after key starts with a digit, ., - or + and is not a whole number of milliseconds ("1.5", "-5", and also "5abc", which XState would read as the name of a delay); an invoke has no string src; entering a state by default leads back to it; an implementation holds an empty function; an entry of implementations::inputs or implementations::outputs names what it may not;

  • errc::unknown_target when a transition, an initial or a history state’s target names no state;

  • errc::unknown_guard when a guard the config names is not in implementations::guards;

  • errc::unknown_delay when an after key names no entry of implementations::delays;

  • errc::unknown_actor when an invoke’s src, or the src of a spawn_child_action the config names, is not in implementations::actors.

Note

Nodes are built in document order, a parent before its children, and the children in the order JavaScript enumerates the keys of states, which is XState’s order; transitions are formatted once every node exists, because a target may name any id.

Return Value

The machine, or the error that refused the config.

Parameters

Name Description

config

The config, a JSON object.

registry

The implementations the config’s names stand for.

See Also

"Creating a machine", in the guide.

"The config", in the guide.

"What creation refuses", in the guide.

"A config is refused when it is created", in the guide.

webcpp::xstate::create_machine_from_definition

Loads a machine back from a definition, with the implementations and the context, which a definition does not hold.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/definition.hpp>

result<machine>
create_machine_from_definition(
    boost::json::value const& definition,
    implementations registry,
    boost::json::value context);

Description

The definition is one to_json, or XState’s machine.toJSON(), wrote. A definition also leaves out the eventless transitions and a history state’s default target, and one that XState wrote leaves out the higher-order guards as well; two states may share an id when a key holds a dot. The loader drops every entry or exit action of the type xstate.raise or xstate.cancel, since the raise and the cancel an after adds are written so and the after it rebuilds adds them again; an entry or exit action the config named so is lost with them. A machine loaded from the definition of one that has none of those takes the original’s steps, and its to_json writes what the original’s writes, the version and the meta and description of each initial included. A node’s key, order and transitions in the definition are not read.

Return Value

The machine; errc::invalid_config when definition is not an object, or a node’s states is not an object of objects, its on not an object of lists of objects, its entry or exit not a list, its invoke not a list of objects, or the first target of its initial not a string, a member of another type than XState writes; or any error of create_machine for the config it rebuilds, which checks what the other members put there, such as a node’s id, type and tags.

Parameters

Name Description

definition

The definition, as to_json writes it.

registry

The implementations the definition’s names stand for.

context

The machine’s initial context.

See Also

"The definition", in the guide.

webcpp::xstate::resolve_state

Builds the snapshot of a state value, completed to every node it implies, with a context.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/snapshot.hpp>

result<snapshot>
resolve_state(
    machine const& owner,
    boost::json::value const& state_value,
    boost::json::value context);

Description

It ports XState’s machine.resolveState({ value, context }). The value is completed with a compound state’s initial child, a parallel state’s regions and every ancestor. The snapshot’s status is status::done when the value is in a final state at the top level and status::active otherwise; it has no output, no history and no children. Its snapshot::nodes are in the order XState’s resolveState gives them, which for a parallel state differs from the order a microstep gives: each level’s named children before their descendants, so the done value {"a": "a2", "b": "b2"} of a parallel root p gives p, p.a, p.b, p.a.a2, p.b.b2.

The keys of an object value are read in the order JavaScript enumerates them, as XState’s getStateNodes reads Object.keys: of a parallel root p with the regions "3" and "z", the value {"z": "z2", "3": "d"} gives p.3 before p.z, and the snapshot’s value is {"3": "d", "z": "z2"}, in both libraries. A string value names a child of the root by its key, as in XState, so "a.b" is the key a.b, not a path; a nested value is written as an object.

Return Value

The snapshot; errc::unknown_state when the value names a state the machine does not have, or is neither a string nor an object.

Parameters

Name Description

owner

The machine.

state_value

The state value, a string or an object.

context

The snapshot’s context.

See Also

"Persisted state", in the guide.

to_json(event const& written);

Description

webcpp::xstate::to_json

Writes a machine’s definition, key for key as XState’s machine.toJSON() writes it.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/definition.hpp>

boost::json::value
to_json(machine const& owner);

Description

For each node it writes its id, key, type, initial, states, history, on, transitions, entry, exit, order (the root’s written -1, as XState writes order || -1), invoke and tags, with its meta, output and description and the config’s version when there are any. A node’s history is written as XState writes it: true as "shallow", a falsy or absent one as false, and any other value as the config gave it. A node’s initial holds the meta and description an object initial gives. The higher-order guards are written where a transition’s config holds them, where XState writes nothing, its guards being functions. What XState’s definition leaves out, this one leaves out too: the context, the eventless transitions and a history state’s default target.

Note

The definition is built deepest first, so each node’s children are written before it.

Return Value

The definition of the root, which holds every node’s.

Parameters

Name Description

owner

The machine.

See Also

"The definition", in the guide.

webcpp::xstate::init_event_type

The type of the event every initial macrostep runs with, "xstate.init".

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/event.hpp>

inline constexpr std::string_view init_event_type = "xstate.init";

Description

It ports XState’s XSTATE_INIT. The event carries the machine’s input as its member input when the input is not null.

Note

For an event of this type that a caller passes to begin, the two libraries differ: XState’s macrostep takes no transition for it, only the eventless transitions it then finds enabled, while xstate’s begin takes its transitions as any event’s.

webcpp::xstate::wildcard

The descriptor that matches every event, "*".

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/event.hpp>

inline constexpr std::string_view wildcard = "*";

Description

It ports XState’s WILDCARD. A state’s transitions under the on key "*" are candidates for any event, after those under the event’s own type and those under a longer partial descriptor such as "mouse.*". An event may have the wildcard as its type: a macrostep refuses one it takes from outside with errc::invalid_event, as XState’s development build does, while one the machine raises takes the wildcard transitions.

See Also

"Event descriptors", in the guide.

webcpp::xstate::actor_ref

An actor’s address in its system: webcpp::xactor::actor_ref, brought into this namespace.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/message.hpp>

using xactor::actor_ref;

Description

Its one member, value, is a number, not a handle: it keeps nothing alive, and actor_system::status_of tells whether its actor still runs. Addresses start at 1, and 0 names no actor. It stands for XState’s ActorRef.

webcpp::xstate::budgets

The fuel of one execution of the system: webcpp::xactor::budgets, brought into this namespace.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/xstate/actors/actor_system.hpp>

using xactor::budgets;

Description

Its one member, fuel, is what each execution starts with, and nothing refills it. Every microstep an actor runs costs one unit, and so does every message an actor sends (an event, a child’s construction and its answer, a child’s start, a stop) and every timer it arms. Each host call that delivers opens executions of its own, each with the whole of it.
