An actor whose work the host does, outside the machines: a fetch, a query, a computation. Once started it is a pending host request; the host answers it, and the actor is done with an output or fails with an error, which its parent hears as a done or an error event.

XState: a promise actor, fromPromise(...).
xstate: xstate::host_actor, registered in implementations.actors and answered with actor_system::resolve or reject.
See Host actors and the actor system example.

Host request

A started host actor waiting for its answer: the actor, its parent, its id, its src and its input. A request whose actor has stopped, because its state was left, is no longer pending, and answering it changes nothing.

XState: the call of a fromPromise creator, with its input.
xstate: xstate::host_request, listed by actor_system::host_requests(); resolve and reject refuse one no longer pending with xactor’s invalid_argument.

See Host actors.

Implementations

The functions a config names, registered by name: actions, guards, delays, the actors an invoke or a spawn runs, the initial context, and the inputs and outputs a config cannot hold as values. A config is JSON and holds no function, so every function has a name in the config and a body here.

XState: setup({ actions, actors, guards, delays }), and the functions written in the config.
xstate: xstate::implementations, given to create_machine: the maps actions, actors, guards, delays, inputs (by invoke id) and outputs (by state id), and context.
See Implementations.

Initial state

The child a compound state enters first, which its initial names. A machine starts with its initial macrostep: its first microstep enters the initial states, and what follows from them runs as in any macrostep, with the event xstate.init, which carries a non-null input as its member input.

XState: initial; getInitialSnapshot and initialTransition.
xstate: initial; begin_initial(machine, input), and get_initial_snapshot and initial_transition, which run it to its end.
See Initial states and The initial macrostep.

Input

The data an actor starts with, given by its creator: the host for a root, the parent for a child. A machine reads it to make its initial context.

XState: createActor(machine, { input }), an invoke’s or a spawn’s input, and the context function ({ input }) => ....
xstate: actor_options::input and begin_initial(machine, input); an invoke’s input in the config or implementations.inputs, by invoke id; spawn_child_action::input.
See A machine’s input, Input to an invoked actor and Input to a spawned actor.

Inspector

Callbacks that hear what every actor of a system does, for tools and logs: each actor’s start, each macrostep a machine actor settles with the event that began it, and each event an actor emits. A macrostep that fails where XState’s transition throws, in an implementation or while an action resolves (a claim of a systemId another actor holds, a target that names no actor), is not heard: XState inspects no snapshot then. One that an unhandled error event fails, with actor_failed, is heard, and so is one that a deferred effect fails, with the snapshot the macrostep reached. Like a listener, an inspector runs inside an actor’s turn and may only read the system.

XState: the inspect option of createActor, with inspection events such as @xstate.actor, @xstate.snapshot and @xstate.event.
xstate: xstate::inspector (started, settled, emitted), given to actor_system::inspect.
See Inspection.

Interleaving

The order in which the deliveries of different actors run. Each actor receives what one sender sends it in the order sent, and runs each macrostep as XState does. Across actors the order may differ from XState’s, since xactor queues each delivery where XState delivers it to an idle actor at once: an actor that sends ping twice to a, then once to b, has b handle its event between the two that a handles, where XState runs the three in the order sent. In the same way, when an actor hears from two senders and one send is caused by the other’s, the two may arrive in another order than in XState, and the callbacks of different actors may run in another order too.

XState: none as a term; XState delivers an event to an idle actor at once, nested in its sender’s call.
xstate: xactor’s queues: each delivery waits in its receiver’s mailbox, and the actors with mail take turns, one message each (xactor).
See Interleaving across actors.

Invoke

A child actor that lives as long as a state is active: entering the state starts it, leaving the state stops it. The state’s onDone and onError take the child’s done and error events.

XState: invoke with src, id, input, systemId, onDone, onError and onSnapshot.
xstate: the same in the config, its src a name of implementations.actors; its onDone, onError and onSnapshot are transitions on xstate.done.actor.<id>, xstate.error.actor.<id> and xstate.snapshot.<id>, and the actor layer sends no snapshot event yet. Entering the state returns xstate.spawnChild and leaving it xstate.stopChild. An invoke without an id gets XState’s <index>.<state id>.
See Invoking actors.

Invoked actor

See invoke.

Listener

A callback the host gives an actor system to hear one kind of thing: the snapshots an actor settles in while it is active and the one it is done in, the events it emits, or the custom actions or the logs the actors hand over. A failed actor’s snapshot reaches no listener: status_of and snapshot_of tell the failure. A listener runs inside an actor’s turn. It may read the system, and a call from it that changes the system returns xactor’s invalid_argument and changes nothing, where XState accepts a send from a subscriber and handles it once the update in progress is done (A callback that calls the system back).

XState: actor.subscribe(...), whose error callback hears a failure, and actor.on(...); a running actor runs custom actions and logs itself.
xstate: actor_system::subscribe, on_emitted, on_action and on_log.
See Watching an actor.

Machine

A state machine: a finite set of states, the transitions between them and the actions they run. In xstate, the immutable tree of state nodes a config describes, with the implementations it names. It is created once and never changes, so one machine serves any number of snapshots and actors, and copying it is cheap.

XState: a StateMachine, from createMachine(config) or setup({ ... }).createMachine(config).
xstate: xstate::machine, from create_machine(config, implementations), which returns a result<machine>.
See Machines.

Machine actor

An actor that runs a machine: a root the host creates from a machine, or a child whose src names a machine in the implementations. It receives events, sends events, has children, starts from an input and ends with an output.

XState: the actor createActor(machine) returns, or a child whose src names a machine in setup({ actors }).
xstate: actor_system::create_actor(machine, options), and an xstate::machine_actor in implementations.actors.
See Machine actors.

Machine core

The half of xstate that computes what a machine does, and runs nothing: it creates machines, computes snapshots with XState’s pure functions and the macrostep cursor, holds delayed events in a simulated clock its caller owns, and writes a machine’s definition as JSON. It includes nothing of xactor and runs no actor. It knows XState’s actors as data, and resolves a spawn or a stop into an action for its caller, which the actor layer executes.

XState: its machines and pure functions, transition and the others, which XState’s package holds beside its actors.
xstate: <webcpp/xstate.hpp>, which needs Boost.JSON, Boost.System and the standard library.
See The machine core.

Macrostep

Everything one event does: the microstep of the transitions the event selects, then every microstep that follows, an eventless transition first and a raised event otherwise, until the machine is stable or no longer active. An actor runs one macrostep at a time.

XState: what transition() or actor.send() runs; macrostep is the name of its internal function, after SCXML.
xstate: xstate::macrostep, the cursor that runs one, and macrostep_result (snapshot, actions, microsteps), what it settled in.
See The macrostep cursor and the machine example.

Meta

Static data a state carries for whoever reads the machine, such as the text a view shows in that state: any JSON, which the machine never reads. A description is a string that documents a state for the people who read the machine. A transition may have both too.

XState: meta and description; snapshot.getMeta().
xstate: the same in the config; get_meta(machine, snapshot), the meta of every active node that has one, by node id; state_node::meta and state_node::description. The definition writes them, except a state’s null meta and a state’s description that is not a string, which xstate leaves out (A state’s null meta, and a description that is not a string).
See Meta and descriptions.

Microstep

One step of a macrostep: the transitions selected together, the states they exit and enter, and the actions those return, in one change of the snapshot. The first microstep of a machine enters its initial states.

XState: a [snapshot, actions] pair of getMicrosteps(), and the inspection event @xstate.microstep.
xstate: xstate::microstep (event, transitions, actions, snapshot), from get_microsteps or from one next() of the cursor.
See Microsteps.

Oracle

XState itself, run on xstate’s test cases: every case ported from XState’s tests, or written where they are silent, runs on XState 5.33.2’s development build, and what XState produces is committed as what xstate’s suites must produce, microstep by microstep and actor by actor.

XState: none.
xstate: test/oracle/oracle.mjs, which runs the machine cases, and test/oracle/actors.mjs, which runs the actor cases; b2 libs/xstate/test/oracle//oracle runs them again.
See XState as the oracle and XState as the oracle in Testing.

Output

What a final state or a machine produces when it is done. A final state’s output travels with its done event; the machine’s is its snapshot’s once it is done, and reaches its parent in its done event.

XState: output on a final state or on the machine; snapshot.output.
xstate: output in the config, or implementations.outputs by state id, the root’s id for the machine’s; snapshot::output.
See Output.

Parallel state

A state whose children, its regions, are all active at once, each in a state of its own. Its state value is an object with one key per region. It is done when every region is in a final state.

XState: type: 'parallel'.
xstate: "type": "parallel"; the order of snapshot::nodes, XState’s, decides which region’s eventless transition comes first.
See Parallel states.

Params

The JSON value a config gives one use of an action or a guard, beside its name: {"type": "addRating", "params": {"by": 5}}. Uses of one implementation tell themselves apart by their params, which the implementation reads.

XState: params, a value, or a function of the context and the event computed when the action runs.
xstate: params in the config, always a fixed value, since JSON holds no function; action_args::params, null when the config gives none, and action::params on a returned action.
See Action objects and params.

Parent and child states

A state with states nested in it is their parent, a compound state. It is active while one of its children is, and it enters first the child its initial names. A compound state without initial is refused at creation.

XState: compound states, with states and initial.
xstate: the same; node_type::compound.
See Parent states.

Parked actor

An actor whose execution ran out of fuel in the middle of its work. It keeps what it has not done, its cursor among it, and does nothing until resume() gives it a new execution. The snapshot it publishes is still the last one it settled in. Events that reach it meanwhile wait behind its work. While any actor is parked, the host’s start, send, clock_tick, resolve and reject are checked, held in the order made, and return out_of_fuel; resume() applies them once the parked actors have settled. stop, create_actor, resume, the registrations of callbacks and the queries run at once.

XState: none.
xstate: a host call that leaves one parked returns run_outcome::out_of_fuel; actor_system::resume() continues it.
See Fuel, parking and resume and the fuel example.

Persisted state

A snapshot kept outside the program between two events, in a file or a database, and turned back into a snapshot when the next event comes. xstate keeps the state value and the context: resolve_state completes the value to every node it implies, with the status done when the value puts the machine in a final state and active otherwise, never error. The output, the error, what history states remember and the children are not restored.

XState: machine.resolveState({ value, context }), often of what JSON.stringify(snapshot) wrote; and an actor’s getPersistedSnapshot(), which createActor(machine, { snapshot }) restores with what its history states remember.
xstate: resolve_state(machine, value, context), which returns a result<snapshot> and refuses a value that names no state with unknown_state. xstate has no counterpart of an actor’s persisted snapshot: what history states remember lives only in an xstate::snapshot.
See Persisted state.

Pure transition function

A function that computes what a machine would do, without starting an actor and without running any effect: the next snapshot, and the actions to run.

XState: transition, initialTransition, getNextSnapshot, getInitialSnapshot, getMicrosteps, getInitialMicrosteps; when a step invokes or spawns, the snapshot they return holds the child as an actor, created and not started.
xstate: transition, initial_transition, get_next_snapshot, get_initial_snapshot, get_microsteps, get_initial_microsteps, each the cursor run to its end, without a bound; a snapshot holds a child as data, its id and its src.
See Computing the next state.

Raised event

An event a machine sends itself. Without a delay, it goes to the macrostep’s internal queue and is taken, in a microstep of its own, once no eventless transition is enabled, before the macrostep settles: no other event comes in between. With a delay, it is a delayed event.

XState: raise(event).
xstate: raise_action, returned as xstate.raise; the internal queue is part of the cursor, so a copy of the cursor has it too.
See Raise.

Region

One child of a parallel state, active with all its siblings. See parallel state.

Root actor

An actor the host created, which has no parent. The host stops it, and its whole family with it; a child is stopped only by its parent. A root created without an id is named x:<n>, as XState names an actor by its session id.

XState: the actor createActor returns, actor.stop() and actor.sessionId.
xstate: actor_system::create_actor and stop(root); parent_of holds nothing for it, and id_of gives its id.
See Creating an actor and Options.

Run to completion

The rule that an actor handles an event entirely, its whole macrostep, before it takes the next one. Events that arrive meanwhile wait, in the order they arrived.

XState: the same rule, as SCXML states it.
xstate: the same for every actor, a macrostep parked for fuel included.
See Messages and mailboxes and How the layer runs.

Self-transition

A transition that stays in its source state: one without a target, one whose target is the source, or one that re-enters the source, its target the source and reenter: true. Only the re-entering kind leaves the source, so only it runs the source’s exit and entry actions and restarts its invoked actors. One whose target is the source leaves the source’s children and enters them again at their initial states; one without a target leaves nothing.

XState: the same three kinds.
xstate: the same; transition_definition::target and reenter.
See Self-transitions and reenter.

Send

The built-in actions that send an event to another actor: sendTo, sendParent, and forwardTo, which sends on the event being handled. A target is a string: a child’s id, or #_ and the id; #_parent; #_internal, the actor itself; or #system: and a systemId.

XState: sendTo(target, event, options), sendParent(event) and forwardTo(target); a target may be a function, such as ({ system }) => system.get(id).
xstate: send_to_action, send_parent_action and forward_to_action, each returned as xstate.sendTo; a function cannot be JSON, so a systemId is named as #system:<systemId>.
See Sending to other actors and Sending events between actors.

Settled

Said of a macrostep that has nothing left to do: no eventless transition is enabled and no raised event is queued, or the machine is no longer active. The cursor says so on the microstep that settles it, and the snapshot that microstep leaves is the new stable one. An event that selects no transition changes nothing in its own microstep, and the macrostep settles there unless an eventless transition is then enabled, as one whose guard reads that event can be: the eventless transitions are tried after the event’s own microstep, even an empty one.

XState: none; XState’s loop ends there.
xstate: progress::settled and macrostep::done(); in the actor layer, run_outcome::settled says that no actor was left parked.
See One microstep at a time.

Snapshot

Where a machine is, as a value: its state value, its context, its status, its output or its error, its active state nodes, what its history states remember, its tags and its children. A macrostep starts from one snapshot and settles in another; none changes in place. A snapshot can be kept, copied and stored.

XState: a MachineSnapshot, from getInitialSnapshot, transition or actor.getSnapshot().
xstate: xstate::snapshot; in the actor layer, actor_system::snapshot_of(actor), which an actor publishes once its macrostep settles.
See The snapshot and Snapshots and status.

Spawn

Starting a child actor with an action rather than with a state: the child lives until a stopChild stops it, or until its parent is done or stopped.

XState: spawnChild(src, { id, systemId, input }), and spawn inside an assign.
xstate: spawn_child_action (src, id, system_id, input), returned as xstate.spawnChild; a spawn without an id keys the child under "", and xstate has no spawn inside an assign yet.
See Spawning actors.

State

A mode a machine can be in, which decides how it reacts to events: a light is green, yellow or red. A machine is in one state at a time, or in one state of each region of its parallel states.

XState: a state node of the config.
xstate: a key of states in the config, held as a state node.
See Finite states.

State machine

See machine.

State node

One node of a machine’s tree: the root, or an atomic, compound, parallel, final or history state, with its transitions, actions, invokes and tags. Its id is the config’s id, or the machine’s id and the node’s path joined by dots (light.green), which a target names with a #.

XState: a StateNode; machine.getStateNodeById(id).
xstate: xstate::state_node, named by its index, its place in document order; machine::node(index) and machine::node_by_id(id).
See State nodes and ids.

State value

A snapshot’s description of its active states, as JSON: a string when the machine’s active state has no children ("green"), an object for nested and parallel states ({"red": "walk"}). A snapshot matches a state value when it is in that state, or in a state within it.

XState: snapshot.value, snapshot.matches(value) and matchesState.
xstate: snapshot::value, a boost::json::value; snapshot::matches and matches_state.
See The state value and Matching a state value.

Statechart

A state machine extended with hierarchy (parent and child states), concurrency (parallel states), history, and communication with other actors. XState’s machines are statecharts, run by the algorithm SCXML defines, and so are xstate’s, which port that algorithm from XState.

XState: every machine.
xstate: every machine.
See State machines and statecharts.

Status

Whether a machine still runs: active; done, once it is complete; or error, once a microstep failed (an implementation failed, a sendTo named a child that is not there, a machine whose root is itself a history state needed its default, an event of the type * came from outside) or a child’s error went unhandled. In the actor layer, an actor also fails where XState throws while it resolves an action: a claim of a systemId another actor holds, a sendTo to the parent of a root. An actor of the actor layer also has xactor’s status, which adds stopped.

XState: snapshot.status: 'active', 'done', 'error' or 'stopped'.
xstate: snapshot::status, an xstate::status; actor_system::status_of, an xactor::status.

See When the machine is done, When an implementation fails and Snapshots and status.

systemId

A name an actor is registered under in its actor system, so that any actor of the system reaches it without a chain of parents. It names one actor at a time, from the actor’s creation until it is done, fails or is stopped. A claim of a name another actor holds fails the claiming actor with system_id_taken, and create_actor refuses it.

XState: systemId on an invoke, a spawn or createActor, and system.get(systemId).
xstate: systemId on an invoke, spawn_child_action::system_id and actor_options::system_id; actor_system::get(system_id); the target #system:<systemId>.
See The system and the actor system example.

Tag

A label on a state, which a snapshot carries while that state is active. Testing a tag, such as busy, keeps working when the states that mean busy change; testing each of those states does not.

XState: tags, and snapshot.hasTag(tag).
xstate: tags in the config; snapshot::tags and snapshot::has_tag(tag).
See Tags.

Target

Where a transition goes: a sibling state’s key, a path below the state starting with a dot (.child), or any state by its id (#light.green); a list of targets enters several regions. A transition without a target stays in its state and runs its actions. A target that names no state is refused at creation with unknown_target.

XState: target.
xstate: target; transition_definition::target, the indexes of the nodes it names.
See Targets and Multiple targets.

Timer

See clock.

Transition

The move from a state to another that an event causes, with the actions it runs on the way. Transitions are deterministic: a state, an event and a context always lead to the same next state. A transition whose targets are its source or inside it does not leave the source; with reenter: true it leaves the source and enters it again, so the source’s exit and entry actions run and its invoked actors restart. reenter changes nothing for a transition without a target, and a transition to another state leaves its source either way.

XState: on: { event: 'target' }, or target, guard, actions and reenter.
xstate: the same in the config; xstate::transition_definition, which a microstep’s transitions point to.
See Transitions and Self-transitions and reenter.

Twin

The program that does on XState 5.33.2 what a program of this page does on xstate, and prints what it finds the same way. A twin agrees, and prints its program’s output; or it diverges on purpose, and prints what XState does where xstate differs, which Appendix B shows after the program’s output. A program that shows what XState has no counterpart for has no twin, and says why.

XState: none.
xstate: test/oracle/twins/<group>/<name>.mjs, beside a divergent twin’s output, <name>.expected; webcpp’s tools/oracle/twins.py runs them and compares.
See A twin for every example and The XState twins.

Undefined

JavaScript’s value for what is not there, which JSON cannot hold. Where an XState implementation may return undefined, a log’s value, a child’s input or a state’s output, xstate’s returns a std::optional with none, and the member is left out, as XState leaves it out. The event xstate.init carries input only when the input is not null.

XState: undefined.
xstate: none in the result of a value_maker, in host_request::input and in snapshot::output; a null pointer for the value on_log receives.
See undefined in Where xstate differs and When a value is undefined.

Wildcard

See event descriptor.

xactor

The actor system xstate’s actor layer runs on, header-only and single-threaded. Its scheduler holds one first-in first-out mailbox per actor and one first-in first-out queue of the actors that have mail: each turn hands one message to the actor at the front of the queue, which goes back to the end of the queue while its mailbox holds more. A delivery is queued, never nested in its sender’s call, so the same inputs give the same run. Each execution has its fuel, and timers run on a clock the host moves. xactor is a library of webcpp of its own, and knows nothing of xstate. xstate’s machine core includes nothing of xactor and runs no actor: it knows XState’s actors as data, and resolves invokes and spawns into xstate.spawnChild and xstate.stopChild actions for its caller.

XState: none; XState’s actors run on JavaScript’s event loop.
xactor: webcpp::xactor, which <webcpp/xactor.hpp> includes whole; the actor layer’s headers, gathered by <webcpp/xstate/actors.hpp>, include it.
See xactor’s page, The actor layer and How the layer runs.

XState

Stately’s JavaScript library of state machines and actors, which xstate ports at version 5.33.2. Where this page names XState, it means that version. Its npm package, xstate, pinned at 5.33.2 under test/oracle/, is what the oracle and the twins run, on its development build, as XState’s own tests do.

See Overview and How xstate is tested.

xstate

The port of XState’s machines and actors: a header-only C++20 library that loads a machine from the JSON config XState’s createMachine takes, and runs it through XState’s pure functions or as an actor. It has two layers, the machine core and the actor layer. It is one of the libraries of webcpp, beside xactor.

XState: the library it ports.
xstate: webcpp::xstate, under include/webcpp/xstate/.
See Overview and Two layers.

Names that start with xstate.

The library gives these names to the events it makes, to the actions it returns and to the higher-order guards. A config may handle the events like any other, and a caller reads the type and the params of each action.

Name What it is Entry

xstate.init

The event of a machine’s initial macrostep, with a non-null input as its member input.

Initial state

xstate.after.<delay>.<state id>

The event a state’s after raises with that delay.

Delayed transition

xstate.done.state.<state id>

Raised when that compound state’s final child is entered, with the child’s output, or when every region of that parallel state is final.

Done event

xstate.done.actor.<id>

Sent to the parent when its child id is done: output, actorId.

Done event

xstate.error.actor.<id>

Sent to the parent when its child id fails: error, actorId.

Error event

xstate.snapshot.<id>

The event an invoke’s onSnapshot takes. The actor layer sends none yet, so such a transition is taken only for an event of that type a caller sends.

Invoke

xstate.raise

A raise, returned with the params event, and id and delay when it has them.

Raised event

xstate.sendTo

A sendTo, a sendParent or a forwardTo, with targetId, event, and id and delay when it has them.

Send

xstate.cancel

A cancel, with the sendId it drops.

Delayed event

xstate.log

A log, with its value and label when it has them.

Built-in action

xstate.spawnChild

A spawn, or an invoke’s start, with id, src, and input and systemId when it has them.

Spawn, Invoke

xstate.stopChild

A stopChild, or an invoke’s stop, with the id of the child.

Child actor

xstate.emit

An emit, with the event emitted.

Emitted event

xstate.not, xstate.and, xstate.or, xstate.stateIn

The JSON of XState’s higher-order guards, which XState writes as functions.

Guard

The terms in a machine

An order: add counts an item, and checkout goes to checking, whose eventless transitions go on to paying when the guard hasItems passes and back to cart otherwise. paying names a custom action, charge, and raises paid, which enters the final state closed. The program drives each macrostep with the cursor, one microstep per next():

const boost::json::value config = boost::json::parse(R"({
    "id": "order",
    "initial": "cart",
    "context": {"items": 0},
    "states": {
        "cart": {
            "on": {
                "add": {"actions": "count"},
                "checkout": {"target": "checking"}
            }
        },
        "checking": {
            "always": [{"target": "paying", "guard": "hasItems"}, {"target": "cart"}]
        },
        "paying": {"entry": ["charge", "confirm"], "on": {"paid": "closed"}},
        "closed": {"type": "final"}
    }
})");

const xstate::assigner count =
    [](const xstate::action_args& args) -> xstate::result<boost::json::object> {
    const std::optional<std::int64_t> items = items_of(args.context);
    if (!items.has_value()) {
        return xstate::failure<boost::json::object>(xstate::errc::implementation_failed);
    }
    return boost::json::object{{"items", *items + 1}};
};
const xstate::event_maker paid =
    [](const xstate::action_args&) -> xstate::result<xstate::event> {
    return xstate::event{.type = "paid", .payload = {}};
};
const xstate::predicate has_items =
    [](const xstate::action_args& args) -> xstate::result<bool> {
    const std::optional<std::int64_t> items = items_of(args.context);
    if (!items.has_value()) {
        return xstate::failure<bool>(xstate::errc::implementation_failed);
    }
    return *items > 0;
};

xstate::implementations implementations;
implementations.actions.emplace("count", xstate::assign_action{.assignment = count});
implementations.actions.emplace(
    "confirm", xstate::raise_action{.event = paid, .id = std::nullopt, .delay = std::nullopt});
implementations.guards.emplace("hasItems", has_items);

const xstate::result<xstate::machine> order = xstate::create_machine(config, implementations);
if (!order.has_value()) {
    return 1;
}

xstate::snapshot now = xstate::get_initial_snapshot(*order);
std::cout << "initial: " << boost::json::serialize(now.value) << ' '
          << boost::json::serialize(now.context) << ' ' << status_name(now.status) << '\n';
for (const std::string_view type : {"checkout", "add", "checkout"}) {
    xstate::macrostep step =
        xstate::begin(*order, now, xstate::event{.type = std::string(type), .payload = {}});
    std::size_t number = 0;
    while (!step.done()) {
        const xstate::progress made = step.next();
        print(type, ++number, made);
    }
    now = step.result().snapshot;
}

Its helpers: items_of reads the context’s items, status_name names a status, and print writes a microstep from the progress that next() returned, its step.snapshot, step.actions and settled.

/** The count of items an order's context holds, or none when it holds no integer `items`. */
std::optional<std::int64_t> items_of(const boost::json::value& context) {
    const boost::json::object* members = context.if_object();
    const boost::json::value* items = members == nullptr ? nullptr : members->if_contains("items");
    if (items == nullptr || !items->is_int64()) {
        return std::nullopt;
    }
    return items->get_int64();
}

std::string_view status_name(xstate::status status) {
    switch (status) {
        case xstate::status::active: return "active";
        case xstate::status::done: return "done";
        case xstate::status::error: return "error";
    }
    return "unknown";
}

/** Prints where a microstep left the machine and the actions it returned. */
void print(std::string_view label, std::size_t number, const xstate::progress& made) {
    const xstate::snapshot& snapshot = made.step.snapshot;
    std::cout << label << " #" << number << ": " << boost::json::serialize(snapshot.value) << ' '
              << boost::json::serialize(snapshot.context) << ' ' << status_name(snapshot.status)
              << " [";
    std::string_view separator;
    for (const xstate::action& returned : made.step.actions) {
        std::cout << separator << returned.type;
        separator = ", ";
    }
    std::cout << ']' << (made.settled ? " settled" : "") << '\n';
}

It prints:

initial: "cart" {"items":0} active
checkout #1: "checking" {"items":0} active []
checkout #2: "cart" {"items":0} active [] settled
add #1: "cart" {"items":1} active [] settled
checkout #1: "checking" {"items":1} active []
checkout #2: "paying" {"items":1} active [charge, xstate.raise]
checkout #3: "closed" {"items":1} done [] settled

Each line is a microstep, numbered within its event’s macrostep, with the state value, the context and the status it left, and the actions it returned.

  • The first checkout is a macrostep of two microsteps: #1 takes the event’s transition to checking, #2 the eventless transition back to cart, since hasItems is false. Nothing follows, so #2 settles it.

  • add changes the context through the assign count, and returns no action: an assign is never handed back.

  • The second checkout takes three microsteps. #2 is the eventless transition to paying, whose entry returns the custom action charge, for the caller to run, and xstate.raise, the raise of paid, already queued. #3 takes the raised event to closed, a final state: the status is done.

  • settled is what the cursor reports with the last microstep of each macrostep. XState has no cursor: its getMicrosteps returns every microstep of a macrostep at once, and the program’s twin marks the last one, so that it prints the same lines (twin).

  • count and hasItems read items through items_of: on a context without an integer items, each fails with implementation_failed, and the snapshot carries the error.

The terms in an actor system

An app that invokes a host actor to fetch its user, registered under the systemId fetcher. The host finds the request, answers it, and the app’s onDone keeps the output. The fetch is the host’s work: a host actor, which waits until the host answers it, stands where XState runs a promise (host actor):

const boost::json::value config = boost::json::parse(R"({
    "id": "app",
    "initial": "loading",
    "context": {"user": null},
    "states": {
        "loading": {
            "invoke": {
                "id": "fetch",
                "src": "fetchUser",
                "systemId": "fetcher",
                "input": {"userId": 42},
                "onDone": {"target": "ready", "actions": "keepUser"}
            }
        },
        "ready": {}
    }
})");

const xstate::assigner keep_user =
    [](const xstate::action_args& args) -> xstate::result<boost::json::object> {
    const boost::json::value* output = args.event.payload.if_contains("output");
    if (output == nullptr) {
        return xstate::failure<boost::json::object>(xstate::errc::implementation_failed);
    }
    return boost::json::object{{"user", *output}};
};

xstate::implementations implementations;
implementations.actors.emplace("fetchUser", xstate::host_actor{});
implementations.actions.emplace("keepUser", xstate::assign_action{.assignment = keep_user});

const xstate::result<xstate::machine> app = xstate::create_machine(config, implementations);
if (!app.has_value()) {
    return 1;
}

xstate::actor_system system({.fuel = 10'000});
const xstate::result<xstate::actor_ref> actor = system.create_actor(*app);
if (!actor.has_value() || !system.start(*actor).has_value()) {
    return 1;
}
print(system, *actor);
for (const xstate::host_request& request : system.host_requests()) {
    std::cout << "request: " << request.id << ' ' << request.src << ' '
              << boost::json::serialize(request.input.value_or(nullptr)) << '\n';
    std::cout << "fetcher is the request's actor: " << (system.get("fetcher") == request.actor)
              << '\n';
    if (!system.resolve(request, boost::json::object{{"name", "Ana"}}).has_value()) {
        return 1;
    }
}
print(system, *actor);
std::cout << "fetcher is registered: " << system.get("fetcher").has_value() << '\n';

print reads the snapshot the app published, snapshot_of, and its children, the (id, src) of each child it has:

/** Prints the actor's state value, its context and the ids of its children. */
void print(const xstate::actor_system& system, xstate::actor_ref actor) {
    const xstate::snapshot* snapshot = system.snapshot_of(actor);
    if (snapshot == nullptr) {
        return;
    }
    std::cout << "app: " << boost::json::serialize(snapshot->value) << ' '
              << boost::json::serialize(snapshot->context) << " children [";
    std::string_view separator;
    for (const auto& [id, src] : snapshot->children) {
        std::cout << separator << id;
        separator = ", ";
    }
    std::cout << "]\n";
}

It prints:

app: "loading" {"user":null} children [fetch]
request: fetch fetchUser {"userId":42}
fetcher is the request's actor: true
app: "ready" {"user":{"name":"Ana"}} children []
fetcher is registered: false

  • Starting the root actor runs its initial macrostep: the app enters loading, whose invoke starts the child fetch. The child is a host actor, so it becomes a host request with its id, its src and its input.

  • system.get("fetcher") finds the child by its systemId, from anywhere in the system.

  • resolve answers the request: the child is done, and the app receives its done event, xstate.done.actor.fetch, whose output the assign keepUser keeps. Leaving loading stops the invoke, and the child, done, no longer holds its systemId.

Fuel

XState has no fuel, so this program has no twin. The event go takes three microsteps, through two eventless transitions, and each execution has two units of fuel. Creating the actor opens no execution; start, send and resume each open one here.

const boost::json::value config = boost::json::parse(R"({
    "id": "steps",
    "initial": "idle",
    "states": {
        "idle": {"on": {"go": "one"}},
        "one": {"always": "two"},
        "two": {"always": "three"},
        "three": {}
    }
})");
const xstate::result<xstate::machine> steps = xstate::create_machine(config, {});
if (!steps.has_value()) {
    return 1;
}

// Each execution has two units of fuel; start, send and resume each open one, and `go` takes
// three microsteps.
xstate::actor_system system({.fuel = 2});
const xstate::result<xstate::actor_ref> actor = system.create_actor(*steps);
if (!actor.has_value()) {
    return 1;
}
print("start", system.start(*actor), system, *actor);
print("send go", system.send(*actor, xstate::event{.type = "go", .payload = {}}), system,
      *actor);
print("resume", system.resume(), system, *actor);

print tells how each host call ended, from its run_outcome, and shows the snapshot the actor has published:

/** Prints how a host call ended and the snapshot the actor has published. */
void print(std::string_view call, const xstate::result<xstate::run_outcome>& outcome,
           const xstate::actor_system& system, xstate::actor_ref actor) {
    if (!outcome.has_value()) {
        std::cout << call << ": " << outcome.error().message() << '\n';
        return;
    }
    const xstate::snapshot* published = system.snapshot_of(actor);
    std::cout << call << ": "
              << (*outcome == xstate::run_outcome::settled ? "settled" : "out_of_fuel") << ", "
              << (published == nullptr ? "no snapshot" : boost::json::serialize(published->value))
              << '\n';
}

It prints:

start: settled, "idle"
send go: out_of_fuel, "idle"
resume: settled, "three"

The start pays for the one microstep of the initial macrostep. send pays for two of the three microsteps of go, then the actor parks: the call returns out_of_fuel, and the snapshot the actor publishes is still the one it last settled in, "idle". resume gives it a new execution, which pays for the third microstep; the macrostep settles, and the actor publishes "three".

Appendix E: Changelog

What changed in xstate in each version of webcpp, newest first, one line per change. "Unreleased" is what the next version brings. The release notes of every version are on webcpp’s index page.

Unreleased

webcpp 0.1.0

  • Changed the guarantee without exceptions to compiling only, which the lint checks.

  • Added the WEBCPP_XSTATE_NO_EXCEPTIONS configuration macro, defined automatically or by the developer.

  • Added a changelog, the page’s last appendix, with each version’s changes.

  • Changed config.hpp to include <webcpp/config.hpp>, webcpp’s configuration, which the build adds.

  • Added WEBCPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS, which disables xstate’s exceptions with every webcpp library’s.
